newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile rejects $400 mln speculative' investment.
newsitem.headline: Chile rejects $400 mln speculative' investment.

text.p: Chile has rejected about $400 million in planned foreign investments because it considered them speculative, the head of the government's Foreign Investment Committee said.

Chilean officials declined to approve the money under the terms of new official investment codes, which draw a distinction between productive investments and those the government considers merely speculative, said commitee chief Eduardo Moyano. The projects involved buying stocks, bonds and term deposits.
News of the rejection helped lower prices on the Santiago Stock Exchange, brokers said.
Speculative projects worth 400 million have not been approved, Moyano told a news conference.
They are projects aimed at participating in the purchase of stocks, bonds and term deposits with the goal of making profits."
He and Economy Minister Alvaro Garcia announced that new foreign investment in Chile came to $4.5 billion in the first nine months of the year.

The $400 million rejected by the Foreign Investment Committee at a meeting on October 23 could still be invested through the Central Bank, under a different investment law known as Chapter 14, Moyano said. But investments that fall under Chapter 14 are subject to a 30 percent reserve requirement known as the "encaje."
The Foreign Investment Committee announced last week that it would start drawing a distinction between speculative and productive capital and that the former would no longer be free from the encaje.
